paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Psalm 112 starts with "Hallelujah!" and then tells you what kind of person is blessed: the one who fears the LORD and "greatly delights in His commandments." (Psalm 112:1) Not the one who just puts up with them. The one who LIKES them. That's a heart that has decided God's way is the good way, and everything else in the psalm grows out of that one choice.

Look at what grows. This man is generous, he lends freely, and his affairs are guided by justice (Psalm 112:5). He has "scattered abroad his gifts to the poor" (Psalm 112:9), so his hands are open instead of clenched. And when darkness comes, "Light dawns in the darkness for the upright" (Psalm 112:4). I know a little about dark places, and I'm telling you, friend, a light that shows up in the dark is better than a whole kitchen of lamps.

Here's what it means for you. "He does not fear bad news; his heart is steadfast, trusting in the LORD." (Psalm 112:7) The bad news can still come, but it doesn't get to be the boss of your heart. So delight in what God says, open your hands to people who need help, and trust Him when the phone buzzes at a bad hour. That kind of life is steady, and the psalm says it will be "remembered forever." (Psalm 112:6)
